title: Cabin Broadband for the Long Gulf Rotations — Fleet Retrofit Request
abstract: Commercial request from an operator to retrofit high-throughput cabin connectivity across its SOLANO Evo fleet, with a fairing installation that does not cost measurable fuel burn and a cabin fit that does not remove revenue seats.

sections.request: We are losing corporate contracts on our long Gulf to Europe rotations because passengers cannot work in the cabin. Our competitors have had usable broadband for three years. We want it on all our Evo aircraft, and we want it on quickly — our commercial team is asking for the first aircraft before the northern winter season and the whole fleet inside eighteen months. Two things matter to us beyond the service itself. The first is fuel: we are told the antenna fairing costs drag and we will not accept a change that shows up in our block fuel by more than a fraction of a per cent, because on our sectors that becomes real money. The second is the cabin: we will not give up seats or galley space for equipment racks, so whatever goes inside has to fit where something else already is. We would also like the crew to be able to reset the system from the cabin panel rather than calling maintenance.
sections.background: We have run a trial with a portable system on two aircraft and it was not acceptable to passengers on sectors over seven hours. Our Evo aircraft were delivered with the wiring provision but not the equipment. We understand there is already an antenna on the crown of these aircraft for navigation and we would like to know early whether the two can live together, because our previous experience on another type was that they could not and it cost us four months.
sections.expected_outcome: A certified installation across the Evo fleet with a published drag figure, no loss of revenue seats, a cabin crew reset capability, and a clear statement of what it means for the existing crown antenna installation.

type_data.business_justification: Two corporate travel contracts worth a combined 14 MEUR per year were lost in 2025 on cabin connectivity alone; the operator treats the retrofit as a condition of renewal.
